title: Tumor–Virus–Immune Dynamics and T-Cell Exhaustion in Oncolytic Immunovirotherapy: A Model-Informed Translational Review
content: Oncolytic immunovirotherapy combines direct tumor-cell lysis with immune activation, but clinical responses remain variable, and durable survival benefits are not regularly observed. This review considers treatment response as a dynamic process determined by tumor growth, viral infection, antiviral immunity, antitumor immune activation, and T-cell dysfunction. Mathematical models have helped to clarify how viral replication, immune responses, and treatment timing may affect treatment results. However, many models represent immune function only in a simplified form or assume that immune-mediated killing remains relatively stable over time. This review, therefore, proposes an exhaustion-aware conceptual framework that includes uninfected and infected tumor cells, free virions, immune effector cells, and time-dependent T-cell exhaustion. By viewing treatment efficacy as a changing balance between viral amplification, antiviral restriction, antitumor immunity, and progressive immune dysfunction, the framework endorses clinically relevant hypotheses on treatment scheduling, checkpoint blockade, longitudinal monitoring, biomarkers, and patient selection.
